nodes.label: Master Specification for the Political Campaign Game
nodes.norm_label: master specification for the political campaign game

nodes.label: V1 Delivery Validation — 5 August 2026
nodes.rationale: Records the completed quality gate: check, E2E, simulation, audit, production build, service worker, and offline recovery all passed.

nodes.label: Sensitive-Person Content Safety
nodes.rationale: Invented allegations are restricted to fictional actors, while real sensitive facts require a primary source, date, and editorial justification.

nodes.label: Natural Non-Militant French Style
nodes.rationale: Keeps event writing direct, varied, politically neutral, and respectful of protected or vulnerable groups.

nodes.label: Pure Simulation Engine
nodes.rationale: A serializable command-in/state-out engine remains independent of React, the DOM, and browser storage, which supports deterministic testing and reuse.

nodes.label: Eight-Step Decision Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Eligibility, weighted resolution, bounded effects, opponents, electorate, time, selection, and logging execute in a fixed sequence.

nodes.label: Simulation Engine Invariants
nodes.rationale: Bounds, finite numbers, exact vote totals, distinct active finalists, one-shot delayed effects, bounded chains, termination, and migrations protect valid game states.

nodes.label: Campaign Decision Loop
nodes.rationale: Twenty-four pre-first-round decisions, five between-round decisions, and a short government epilogue target a 27–33 decision campaign.

nodes.label: Controlled Randomness
nodes.rationale: Context-sensitive deterministic randomness lets good decisions improve odds without guaranteeing outcomes.

nodes.label: Relative Campaign Success
nodes.rationale: Progress and political legacy matter alongside outright victory so smaller parties can achieve meaningful success.

nodes.label: Implicit Party Difficulty
nodes.rationale: Difficulty emerges from starting position, potential, and rejection rather than an explicit difficulty selector.

nodes.label: Independent Legal and Editorial Review
nodes.rationale: Public publication is gated on an independent review of real-person, attribution, neutrality, privacy, and branding risks.

nodes.label: Versioned Real-World Data Snapshot
nodes.rationale: The V1 avoids live data and stores a dated, reviewable snapshot so editorial provenance remains explicit and gameplay values remain fictional.

nodes.label: V1 Test Validation — 5 August 2026
nodes.rationale: Documents 38 Vitest tests, 18 E2E tests, 1,000 simulations, zero known high-level vulnerabilities, and manual offline/browser verification.

nodes.label: Fictional French Presidential Campaign Simulation
nodes.rationale: The product promises a short narrative strategy game in which roughly thirty decisions shape qualification, victory, and political legacy.

nodes.label: V1 Post-Election Scope Boundary
nodes.rationale: V1 ends after elimination or the second round, with only a brief government-formation epilogue, leaving a future mandate module separate.

nodes.label: Fiction Simulation Disclaimer
nodes.rationale: Makes clear that events, dialogue, probabilities, rankings, and results are fictional and neither official information nor political endorsement.

nodes.label: Legal, Editorial, and Ethical Safety Model
nodes.rationale: Separates fictional gameplay from verifiable real-world context and constrains defamation, attribution, branding, neutrality, and privacy risks.
nodes.norm_label: legal, editorial, and ethical safety model

nodes.label: Configurable Real-Party Names
nodes.rationale: Real party names remain editable data while official logos and copied visual identities are excluded.

nodes.label: Fictional Candidate Model
nodes.rationale: The public-safe mode uses fictional candidates and cadres so narrative freedom does not create claims about identifiable people.

nodes.label: Real Public Figures as Sourced Context
nodes.rationale: Real personalities may appear only as factual, sourced, non-defamatory context, without invented authentic-seeming dialogue.
nodes.norm_label: real public figures as sourced context

nodes.label: Political Neutrality by Design
nodes.rationale: Every political family must have strengths, weaknesses, risks, and viable paths, while gameplay parameters are not framed as moral truth.

nodes.label: Local-Only Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: V1 has no account, server profile, analytics, advertising, or personal-data collection; saves remain on the device.

nodes.label: React-Independent Simulation Architecture
nodes.rationale: The simulation core imports neither React nor DOM/UI components, keeping gameplay logic portable and testable.

nodes.label: IndexedDB Persistence
nodes.rationale: Versioned local storage preserves active runs, archives, achievements, migrations, and recovery without a backend.

nodes.label: Offline-First PWA
nodes.rationale: After the first visit, the complete game remains installable and playable without any required network call.

nodes.label: Six Dashboard Indicators
nodes.rationale: Polling, popularity, mobilization, finances, credibility, and cohesion provide a readable mobile dashboard without exposing the full internal model.

nodes.label: Hidden Campaign Variables
nodes.rationale: Latent support, reserves, rejection, fatigue, loyalty, and other internal values surface through narrative signals rather than a raw spreadsheet.

nodes.label: Rapid Custom-Party Creation
nodes.rationale: A 60–90 second questionnaire derives ideology, organization, signature measures, and target electorate without heavy configuration.

nodes.label: Five Campaign Methods
nodes.rationale: Terrain, presidential stature, rupture, digital campaigning, and unity establish distinct trade-offs at the start of a run.

nodes.label: Deterministic Seeded PRNG
nodes.rationale: The same version, seed, and decisions reproduce the same campaign while different seeds preserve narrative variety.

nodes.label: Contextual Softmax Outcome Resolution
nodes.rationale: Base weights become logits modified by statistics and history, then softmax produces hidden probabilities for a seeded draw.

nodes.label: Weighted Event Selection
nodes.rationale: Phase, date, cooldown, party, ideology, prior events, opponents, chains, rarity, and narrative pacing determine the next event.

nodes.label: Soft Event-Category Quotas
nodes.rationale: Soft quotas prevent repetitive campaigns while retaining variety and non-scripted pacing.

nodes.label: Configurable Campaign Calendar
nodes.rationale: A configurable election date, T−365 start, semi-random intervals, and bounded phases avoid hard-coding a real election year.

nodes.label: Emergent Campaign Program
nodes.rationale: Campaign choices build positions progressively, affect electorate segments, and create contradictions that can return later.

nodes.label: Three-Round Televised Debate
nodes.rationale: Three short rounds combine media skill, thematic competence, consistency, fatigue, opponent aggression, strategy, and chance.

nodes.label: Autonomous Opponent Simulation
nodes.rationale: Every active opponent takes an abstract strategy-driven turn after the player, allowing crises, replacement, alliances, and support changes mostly off-screen.

nodes.label: Twelve Synthetic Electorate Blocs
nodes.rationale: A limited set of synthetic blocs captures political priorities and turnout behavior without a gigantic crossed demographic database.

nodes.label: Latent Electoral Support
nodes.rationale: The engine tracks underlying support by bloc and party using ideology, credibility, rejection, mobilization, events, and strategic voting.

nodes.label: Noisy Poll Model
nodes.rationale: Polls deliberately lag and perturb latent support with sampling error, indecision, house effects, volatility, and rounding.

nodes.label: Simplified Regional Electoral Map
nodes.rationale: Regional strengths are visualized without simulating every municipality; official results remain national.

nodes.label: First-Round Election Calculation
nodes.rationale: Latent support, turnout, strategic voting, bounded election noise, and exact normalization determine two distinct active finalists.

nodes.label: Between-Rounds Vote Transfers
nodes.rationale: Eliminated parties’ voters transfer imperfectly according to ideology, rejection, endorsements, alliances, mobilization, abstention, and campaign history.

nodes.label: Second-Round Election Calculation
nodes.rationale: Bloc transfers, abstention, and final dynamics resolve the duel, while exact ties and recount chains remain exceptionally rare.

nodes.label: Conditional Alliances and Defections
nodes.rationale: Coalitions, dissidence, support, withdrawal, and negotiated roles appear only through context-sensitive events and carry coherence costs.

nodes.label: Narrative and Secret Endings
nodes.rationale: Main endings cover electoral and career outcomes, while very rare fictional alternate-history chains require strong preconditions and avoid glorifying violence.

nodes.label: Campaign Score out of 100
nodes.rationale: Electoral performance, progress, qualification, party growth, coherence, legacy, and special achievements reward historic small-party campaigns as well as wins.

nodes.label: Local Campaign Archives and Pantheon
nodes.rationale: Completed runs, active state, statistics, achievements, scores, parties, endings, and seeds remain locally recoverable, migratable, exportable, and deletable.

nodes.label: Client-Generated Result Share Card
nodes.rationale: Portrait and landscape PNGs are generated without a backend, contain a fiction notice, and exclude official portraits and logos.

nodes.label: Mobile Accessibility and AA Contrast
nodes.rationale: Keyboard access, visible focus, AA contrast, accessible names, touch targets, ARIA announcements, and non-color cues make the mobile-first flow usable.

nodes.label: Layered Testing Stack
nodes.rationale: Unit, property-based, component, E2E, simulation, type, lint, build, browser, and dependency checks jointly protect deterministic gameplay and delivery quality.

nodes.label: Property-Based Simulation Tests
nodes.rationale: Hundreds of generated campaigns search for exceptions, NaN values, invalid totals, infinite chains, blocked runs, and degenerate outcome distributions.

nodes.label: 1,000–10,000 Campaign Balance Simulator
nodes.rationale: Mass local simulation measures qualification, victory, scores, event frequency, dominant choices, invalid states, and run length without forcing artificial party equality.

nodes.label: Custom Political Movement
nodes.rationale: The player can create a configurable movement whose ideology, organization, program, and electorate are derived from concise choices.
